method: Source-first limitation review of all five Catholic-side stages in the 38 previously unassessed debates. Each stage retains actual live English and French text and effective intended citation IDs, plus a scope rule. An original-section check bounds a case's central source-based premise; it does not certify its every sentence, every historical/clinical proposition, or its French fidelity.
limits: Cases mark central primary-document passages as examined only where actually retrieved; otherwise they are flagged without claiming original collation.
Five-stage records are text and evidence-scope assessments, not independent theological certification.
Empirical and psychological facts require their respective current research sources.
Archived CSE055/CSE056/CSE058 remain archived and are not new debates.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Natural-law goods exceed the harm principle; Aquinas does not establish which private conduct civil law must prohibit.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Mill's anti-coercion thesis is not a claim that all consensual acts are morally good.

stages.claim_text_en: Causing unjust harm is a major moral consideration, and not every private preference should be regulated.
stages.claim_text_fr: Causer un tort injuste est une considération morale majeure, et toute préférence privée ne doit pas être réglementée.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The illicit inference is from limits on public coercion to the claim that avoiding harm exhausts personal morality. Whether the state may prohibit an act is distinct from whether someone should choose it. Fidelity, self-mastery and freely assumed obligations require moral examination even where civil prohibition would be unjustified.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le saut illégitime consiste à déduire des limites de la contrainte publique que l’absence de dommage épuise la morale personnelle. Que l’État puisse interdire un acte est distinct de la question de savoir si quelqu’un devrait le choisir. Fidélité, maîtrise de soi et obligations librement assumées demandent un examen moral même si une interdiction civile serait injustifiée.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: Catholic ethics asks not only who is harmed, but what kind of act is deliberately chosen and which human goods it respects or contradicts. Sexuality is judged in relation to chastity, marriage, fidelity and procreation, not by a harm test alone.
stages.claim_text_fr: La morale catholique demande non seulement qui est lésé, mais quel type d’acte est délibérément choisi et quels biens humains il respecte ou contredit. La sexualité est jugée en relation avec la chasteté, le mariage, la fidélité et la procréation, non par le seul critère du dommage.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Fidelity, rational self-mastery, marriage and care for children are intelligible human goods, not duties arising only from Church membership (Aquinas, I-II q.94 a.2). Whether a particular choice contradicts them depends on the moral object deliberately chosen (Veritatis Splendor §78). Even conduct judged morally wrong does not automatically warrant civil prohibition.
stages.claim_text_fr: La fidélité, la maîtrise rationnelle de soi, le mariage et le soin des enfants sont des biens humains intelligibles, non des devoirs nés de la seule appartenance à l’Église (saint Thomas, I-II, q.94, a.2). Qu’un choix particulier les contredise dépend de l’objet moral délibérément choisi (Veritatis Splendor, §78). Même une conduite jugée moralement mauvaise ne justifie pas automatiquement son interdiction civile.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Harm matters, but it is not the whole of morality. The decisive question is whether the chosen act respects the goods that make human sexuality intelligible.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le dommage compte, mais il n’épuise pas la morale. La question décisive est de savoir si l’acte choisi respecte les biens qui donnent sens à la sexualité humaine.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Moral object, intention and circumstances are distinct from the bare presence of consent.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Planned Parenthood's consent standard must not be misrepresented as a comprehensive moral theory.

stages.claim_text_en: Consent is necessary. Without it, the injustice can be severe.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le consentement est nécessaire. Sans lui, l’injustice peut être grave.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: Consent is necessary, but agreement does not by itself make the chosen act just. Two consenting persons can betray an existing spouse, exploit vulnerability, or agree to something contrary to a serious duty. The moral object and obligations remain relevant (Veritatis Splendor §§78–80).
stages.claim_text_fr: Le consentement est nécessaire, mais l’accord ne rend pas à lui seul l’acte choisi juste. Deux personnes consentantes peuvent trahir un conjoint, exploiter une vulnérabilité ou convenir de quelque chose de contraire à un devoir grave. L’objet moral et les obligations demeurent déterminants (Veritatis Splendor, §§78–80).
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: Two people can consent to adultery, to an exploitative commercial arrangement, or to conduct that violates a prior promise. Catholic ethics therefore asks two questions: Was it freely chosen? And what exactly was chosen?
stages.claim_text_fr: Deux personnes peuvent consentir à l’adultère, à un arrangement commercial exploiteur ou à une conduite qui viole une promesse antérieure. La morale catholique pose donc deux questions : l’acte a-t-il été librement choisi ? Et qu’a-t-on exactement choisi ?
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Then the dispute moves from consent to the nature of sexual union itself: whether sexual acts have goods and meanings that are not created solely by agreement. Catholicism says they do, especially through their relation to marriage and generation.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le débat se déplace alors du consentement vers la nature même de l’union sexuelle : les actes sexuels ont-ils des biens et des significations qui ne sont pas créés uniquement par l’accord ? Le catholicisme répond oui, notamment en raison de leur rapport au mariage et à la génération.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Consent is indispensable, but it cannot make every chosen act good. It answers who chose; it does not by itself answer whether the choice was good.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le consentement est indispensable, mais il ne peut rendre bon tout acte choisi. Il répond à la question de savoir qui a choisi ; il ne suffit pas à dire si le choix était bon.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: A benign intended end does not automatically justify a deliberately chosen wrong means.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Fletcher's complete original book is still not collated; reconstructed opposition is not verbatim.

stages.claim_text_en: Catholic morality fully agrees that intention is one essential part of a human act and can increase or lessen responsibility.
stages.claim_text_fr: La morale catholique reconnaît pleinement que l’intention est une dimension essentielle de l’acte humain et peut augmenter ou diminuer la responsabilité.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The error is making intention the only source of moral goodness. A good end does not automatically make the chosen means good.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’erreur consiste à faire de l’intention l’unique source de bonté morale. Une bonne fin ne rend pas automatiquement bon le moyen choisi.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: The tradition distinguishes the object chosen, the further intention and the circumstances. A person can sincerely seek a good end and still choose a means that contradicts another serious good.
stages.claim_text_fr: La tradition distingue l’objet choisi, l’intention ultérieure et les circonstances. Une personne peut sincèrement rechercher une bonne fin tout en choisissant un moyen qui contredit un autre bien grave.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: They are connected but not identical. The same desired end can be pursued by different means, and moral reasoning routinely distinguishes between them. Wanting to save a relationship, avoid pregnancy or relieve distress does not tell us which act was chosen to achieve that end.
stages.claim_text_fr: Ils sont liés mais non identiques. La même fin désirée peut être poursuivie par des moyens différents, et le raisonnement moral les distingue constamment. Vouloir sauver une relation, éviter une grossesse ou soulager une détresse ne dit pas quel acte a été choisi pour y parvenir.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Good intentions matter greatly, but they do not erase the moral character of the means deliberately chosen.
stages.claim_text_fr: Les bonnes intentions comptent beaucoup, mais elles n’effacent pas le caractère moral des moyens délibérément choisis.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Intrinsically wrong chosen objects cannot be made good by proportional calculation.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Fletcher's full primary work has not been examined; serious argument about a particular object is still needed.

stages.claim_text_en: Catholic morality agrees that circumstances and culpability can radically change how responsible a person is.
stages.claim_text_fr: La morale catholique reconnaît que les circonstances et la culpabilité peuvent modifier radicalement la responsabilité d’une personne.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: Fletcher correctly notes that circumstances affect the morality of choices; his stronger claim that love can override every negative precept is incompatible with intrinsically evil acts. Veritatis Splendor §§79–81 locates their wrongness in the object freely chosen, not in a failure to calculate the most loving result.
stages.claim_text_fr: Fletcher relève à juste titre que les circonstances comptent dans les choix ; mais l’idée que l’amour puisse écarter toute interdiction morale contredit l’existence d’actes intrinsèquement mauvais. Veritatis Splendor (§§79–81) situe leur malice dans l’objet librement choisi, non dans l’absence d’un calcul du résultat le plus aimant.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: An intrinsically evil act is one whose chosen object is incompatible with the good of the person in every case. The doctrine concerns the act’s moral species, not a claim that every person who commits it is equally guilty.
stages.claim_text_fr: Un acte intrinsèquement mauvais est un acte dont l’objet choisi est incompatible avec le bien de la personne dans tous les cas. La doctrine concerne l’espèce morale de l’acte, non l’affirmation que toute personne qui le commet est également coupable.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Only if no argument is offered for why the object is always incompatible with the good. The real work is identifying the moral object correctly and showing why it cannot be ordered to a good end. “Intrinsic evil” is the conclusion of that analysis, not a substitute for it.
stages.claim_text_fr: Seulement si aucun argument n’est donné pour montrer pourquoi l’objet est toujours incompatible avec le bien. Le vrai travail consiste à identifier correctement l’objet moral et à montrer pourquoi il ne peut être ordonné à une bonne fin. « Intrinsèquement mauvais » est la conclusion de l’analyse, non son substitut.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Absolute norms do not deny complexity. They distinguish the objective character of a choice from the often much more complex question of personal culpability.
stages.claim_text_fr: Les normes absolues ne nient pas la complexité. Elles distinguent le caractère objectif d’un choix de la question, souvent bien plus complexe, de la culpabilité personnelle.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Gospel and Pauline sexual teachings supply principles beyond a list of modern technology names.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Original verse-to-source deep links and original-language exegesis require distinct verification.

stages.claim_text_en: Many modern practices are not named in the Gospels, and a serious Christian argument cannot pretend otherwise.
stages.claim_text_fr: De nombreuses pratiques modernes ne sont pas nommées dans les Évangiles, et un argument chrétien sérieux ne peut prétendre le contraire.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The hidden premise is that Christian morality is limited to a list of behaviors explicitly named by Jesus. The New Testament itself does not work that way.
stages.claim_text_fr: La prémisse cachée est que la morale chrétienne se limite à une liste de comportements explicitement nommés par Jésus. Le Nouveau Testament lui-même ne fonctionne pas ainsi.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: Christ condemns adultery and deliberate lust (Mt 5:27–28) and teaches the lasting significance of marriage (Mt 19:3–9). St Paul reasons from the body's belonging to Christ when treating sexual conduct (1 Cor 6:12–20). These texts provide enduring premises, while distinct arguments must still show how each modern intervention relates to them; Scripture does not name IVF or contraception as technologies.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le Christ condamne l’adultère et la convoitise délibérée (Mt 5, 27–28) et enseigne la portée durable du mariage (Mt 19, 3–9). Saint Paul fonde ses enseignements sexuels sur l’appartenance du corps au Christ (1 Co 6, 12–20). Ces textes offrent des principes durables, mais une argumentation distincte doit montrer leur application à chaque intervention moderne ; l’Écriture ne nomme pas la FIV ni la contraception comme techniques.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: An act's absence from the Gospel vocabulary cannot prove permission or prohibition. Its object must be identified and assessed through Scripture, natural law and the precise subsequent teaching concerning that act; a general appeal to Jesus is not a substitute for this demonstration.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’absence du nom d’un acte dans les Évangiles ne prouve ni sa permission ni son interdiction. Il faut identifier son objet et l’examiner à la lumière de l’Écriture, de la loi naturelle et des enseignements précis qui le concernent ; une référence générale à Jésus ne remplace pas cette démonstration.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: “Jesus never used this word” is not enough. The real question is whether the later norm follows from the moral principles Christianity actually received.
stages.claim_text_fr: « Jésus n’a jamais utilisé ce mot » ne suffit pas. La vraie question est de savoir si la norme ultérieure découle des principes moraux réellement reçus par le christianisme.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Paul grounds moral imperatives in union with Christ, the body and sanctification.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Historical-cultural interpretation remains an exegetical argument, not self-certifying from citation.

stages.claim_text_en: Paul wrote in a particular culture, so exegesis must distinguish local custom from the reasons he gives for a moral norm.
stages.claim_text_fr: Paul écrivait dans une culture particulière ; l’exégèse doit donc distinguer les usages locaux des raisons qu’il donne pour une norme morale.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: A cultural setting by itself does not make a moral teaching culturally relative. One must show that Paul’s stated reasons depend on a premise we now know to be false or merely local.
stages.claim_text_fr: Un contexte culturel ne rend pas à lui seul un enseignement moral culturellement relatif. Il faut montrer que les raisons données par Paul dépendent d’une prémisse que nous savons aujourd’hui fausse ou purement locale.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: In 1 Corinthians 6:13–20, St Paul argues from union with Christ, the Holy Spirit's dwelling in the body and the body's redemption. In 1 Thessalonians 4:3–8, he appeals to sanctification and God's call. These are theological premises, not simply a demand to imitate the social etiquette of his century; creation-language arguments elsewhere require their own textual references.
stages.claim_text_fr: Dans 1 Corinthiens 6, 13–20, saint Paul raisonne à partir de l’union au Christ, de la présence de l’Esprit Saint dans le corps et de la rédemption du corps. Dans 1 Thessaloniciens 4, 3–8, il invoque la sanctification et l’appel de Dieu. Ce sont des prémisses théologiques, non de simples prescriptions d’étiquette antique ; les arguments tirés de la création dans d’autres passages exigent leurs propres références.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Historical exegesis can reveal culturally conditioned assumptions. To overturn a particular moral conclusion, however, one must identify the relevant premise, establish that it is culturally contingent or false, and show that the conclusion depends upon it. The age of Paul's letter is not itself such a demonstration.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’exégèse historique peut révéler des présupposés conditionnés par la culture. Pour renverser une conclusion morale déterminée, il faut toutefois identifier la prémisse décisive, établir son caractère contingent ou erroné et montrer que la conclusion en dépend. L’ancienneté d’une lettre de Paul ne suffit pas à cette démonstration.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Context must be studied, but culture alone does not dissolve an argument. The question is whether Paul’s reasons survive historical scrutiny.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le contexte doit être étudié, mais la culture seule ne dissout pas un argument. La question est de savoir si les raisons de Paul résistent à l’examen historique.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Magisterial development does not make intrinsically wrong choices permissible by changing vocabulary.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Complete century-by-century comparison requires multiple historical witnesses, not only Veritatis Splendor.

stages.claim_text_en: Terminology, discipline, canonical penalties, pastoral strategies and applications do change. Development is real.
stages.claim_text_fr: La terminologie, la discipline, les peines canoniques, les stratégies pastorales et les applications changent. Le développement est réel.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The possibility that a non-definitive judgment could require correction does not establish that any particular doctrine has been reversed. A proposed contradiction must identify the same moral proposition, the relevant qualifications and the authority with which each text teaches it (Veritatis Splendor §53).
stages.claim_text_fr: La possibilité qu’un jugement non définitif exige une correction ne prouve pas qu’une doctrine déterminée ait été renversée. Une contradiction alléguée doit identifier la même proposition morale, ses qualifications pertinentes et le degré d’autorité de chaque texte (Veritatis Splendor, §53).
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: The continuity chain is substantial: New Testament teaching on adultery, fornication and marriage; the Roman Catechism; and later papal teaching such as Casti Connubii. Newer documents often refine concepts or apply them to new technology rather than inventing the underlying norm.
stages.claim_text_fr: La chaîne de continuité est substantielle : enseignement du Nouveau Testament sur l’adultère, la fornication et le mariage ; Catéchisme romain ; puis enseignement pontifical tel que Casti Connubii. Les documents plus récents précisent souvent les concepts ou les appliquent à de nouvelles technologies plutôt que d’inventer la norme sous-jacente.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Historical change may concern discipline, formulation, application or an authoritative judgment of differing weight. It is not enough to place two documents from different centuries side by side: the propositions must actually conflict, not merely concern different moral objects or historical conditions. Permanent negative norms concerning intrinsically evil acts remain affirmed in Veritatis Splendor §§79–83.
stages.claim_text_fr: Un changement historique peut concerner la discipline, la formulation, l’application ou un jugement doté d’une autorité différente. Juxtaposer deux documents de siècles différents ne suffit pas : leurs propositions doivent réellement se contredire et non porter sur des objets moraux ou des conditions distincts. Veritatis Splendor (§§79–83) réaffirme la permanence des interdictions d’actes intrinsèquement mauvais.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Historical development is real, but it does not make every moral norm provisional. The alleged contradiction must be demonstrated at the level of the same moral proposition.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le développement historique est réel, mais il ne rend pas toute norme morale provisoire. La contradiction alléguée doit être démontrée au niveau de la même proposition morale.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.original_locator: I-II q.77 aa.6–8; I-II q.78; CCC 2352
cases.claim_supported_only_within: Passion and vice affect voluntariness differently; grave matter is not identical with proven subjective mortal guilt.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Personal diagnosis of compulsion or culpability cannot be inferred from a generic source.

stages.claim_text_en: Knowledge and freedom can be reduced by fear, anxiety, immaturity or an acquired habit. Yet not every habitual choice is involuntary: the degree of deliberation in the concrete act remains decisive (Aquinas I–II qq.77–78; Catechism §2352).
stages.claim_text_fr: La connaissance et la liberté peuvent être diminuées par la peur, l’anxiété, l’immaturité ou une habitude acquise. Tout acte habituel n’est pourtant pas involontaire : le degré de délibération dans l’acte concret demeure déterminant (saint Thomas, I–II, q.77–78 ; Catéchisme, §2352).
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: A strong habit may impede freedom without abolishing it. Aquinas distinguishes sin from prior passion (I–II q.77) from sin through knowingly chosen vice (q.78); those are not identical. Scientific literature about drug addiction cannot establish a sexual-addiction diagnosis or determine someone's moral guilt.
stages.claim_text_fr: Une habitude forte peut entraver la liberté sans l’abolir. Saint Thomas distingue le péché sous l’effet d’une passion préalable (I–II, q.77) de celui qui procède d’un vice sciemment choisi (q.78) ; ces situations ne sont pas identiques. Les recherches sur la toxicomanie ne prouvent ni un diagnostic de dépendance sexuelle ni la culpabilité morale d’une personne.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: Traditional moral analysis therefore asks about actual knowledge and freedom in the concrete act, while also considering how the habit developed and whether the person resists or reinforces it.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’analyse morale traditionnelle examine donc la connaissance et la liberté effectives dans l’acte concret, tout en considérant comment l’habitude s’est formée et si la personne y résiste ou la renforce.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Often it is difficult, which is why categorical judgments about another person’s mortal guilt are unsafe. Difficulty of measuring culpability, however, does not change the objective moral character of the act.
stages.claim_text_fr: C’est souvent difficile, raison pour laquelle les jugements catégoriques sur la culpabilité mortelle d’autrui sont imprudents. Mais la difficulté de mesurer la culpabilité ne change pas le caractère moral objectif de l’acte.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Habit can reduce responsibility, but not automatically. Objective act and subjective culpability must remain distinct.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’habitude peut réduire la responsabilité, mais pas automatiquement. L’acte objectif et la culpabilité subjective doivent rester distincts.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Aquinas defines chastity as rational governance of desire rather than hatred of sexual desire.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Freud 1908 is historical psychological theory, not evidence of modern clinical causal effects.

stages.claim_text_en: Bad formation can become repressive. Sexual desire is part of human nature and is not itself sinful.
stages.claim_text_fr: Une mauvaise formation peut devenir répressive. Le désir sexuel appartient à la nature humaine et n’est pas en lui-même pécheur.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: Restraint of desire is not equivalent to repression. Mature human agency includes ordering powerful desires rather than simply expressing them whenever they arise.
stages.claim_text_fr: La maîtrise du désir n’équivaut pas à la répression. L’action humaine mûre implique d’ordonner des désirs puissants plutôt que de les exprimer chaque fois qu’ils surgissent.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: In Catholic virtue ethics, chastity is integration under reason: married and unmarried people both learn to direct sexuality according to their state and duties. The goal is not numbness but freedom from being ruled by appetite.
stages.claim_text_fr: Dans l’éthique catholique des vertus, la chasteté est une intégration sous la raison : mariés et célibataires apprennent à orienter la sexualité selon leur état et leurs devoirs. Le but n’est pas l’insensibilité, mais la liberté à l’égard de la domination de l’appétit.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: An education based on panic, shame or repression can aggravate suffering, which must be taken seriously. But Freud's 1908 causal theory is not a contemporary clinical demonstration that Catholic chastity itself causes illness. Chastity in Aquinas (II–II q.151 a.1) is a virtue ordering desire through reason, not contempt for the body; psychological care remains appropriate where distress is real.
stages.claim_text_fr: Une éducation fondée sur la panique, la honte ou le refoulement peut aggraver la souffrance, qu’il faut prendre au sérieux. Mais la théorie causale de Freud en 1908 n’est pas une démonstration clinique contemporaine selon laquelle la chasteté catholique cause elle-même des maladies. Chez saint Thomas (II–II, q.151, a.1), la chasteté ordonne le désir par la raison, sans mépris du corps ; un accompagnement psychologique reste approprié lorsque la souffrance est réelle.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Chastity is not the denial of sexuality. Properly understood, it is the discipline by which sexuality serves the good of the person rather than governing the person.
stages.claim_text_fr: La chasteté n’est pas la négation de la sexualité. Bien comprise, elle est la discipline par laquelle la sexualité sert le bien de la personne au lieu de la gouverner.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Consecrated virginity has a positive theological meaning and does not imply marriage is impure.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: A papal treatment of chastity does not prove that every celibate person is psychologically healthy.

stages.claim_text_en: Celibacy is not automatically healthy. Isolation, poor formation, emotional immaturity or lack of community can seriously damage a person.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le célibat n’est pas automatiquement sain. L’isolement, une mauvaise formation, l’immaturité affective ou l’absence de communauté peuvent gravement nuire à une personne.

stages.claim_text_en: The need for intimacy and attachment does not establish that sexual activity itself is a psychological necessity.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le besoin d’intimité et d’attachement n’établit pas que l’activité sexuelle elle-même soit une nécessité psychologique.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: Catholic tradition treats continence as humanly possible while insisting on friendship, community, prayer and disciplined life. It distinguishes the need for love and relationship from a supposed necessity of sexual expression.
stages.claim_text_fr: La tradition catholique considère la continence comme humainement possible tout en insistant sur l’amitié, la communauté, la prière et une vie disciplinée. Elle distingue le besoin d’amour et de relation d’une prétendue nécessité d’expression sexuelle.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: That is a theological question distinct from psychological health. Catholicism values consecrated virginity because of its undivided dedication to God, not because marriage or sexuality are dirty.
stages.claim_text_fr: C’est une question théologique distincte de la santé psychologique. Le catholicisme valorise la virginité consacrée en raison de son dévouement sans partage à Dieu, non parce que le mariage ou la sexualité seraient impurs.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: A 15-person qualitative study cannot establish the prevalence or cause of psychological distress among all celibates. Celibacy is not a psychiatric diagnosis; each person's health, relationships and support need individual assessment.
stages.claim_text_fr: Une étude qualitative de quinze personnes ne permet d'établir ni la prévalence ni la cause de la détresse chez tous les célibataires. Le célibat n'est pas un diagnostic psychiatrique ; la santé, les relations et le soutien de chacun exigent un examen individuel.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Scandal and occasions of sin are analytically distinct from the objective nature of cohabitation.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Psychological or statistical claims about cohabitation outcomes need separate empirical evidence.

stages.claim_text_en: Couples should learn one another’s habits, expectations, weaknesses and practical compatibility before marriage.
stages.claim_text_fr: Les couples doivent apprendre à connaître les habitudes, les attentes, les faiblesses et la compatibilité pratique de l’autre avant le mariage.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: Simulating married life is not established as the best or necessary way to discern marriage. Sexual relations, shared housing, scandal and practical dependence are also distinct moral questions and should not be collapsed into one.
stages.claim_text_fr: Simuler la vie conjugale n’est pas établi comme le meilleur ni le seul moyen de discerner le mariage. Les relations sexuelles, le logement commun, le scandale et la dépendance pratique sont aussi des questions morales distinctes qui ne doivent pas être confondues.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: If cohabitation includes sex, Catholic teaching judges the sexual relations as outside marriage. If it is genuinely continent, sharing a residence is not itself fornication, but the couple must still assess proximate occasion, scandal and whether financial or emotional entanglement makes discernment less free.
stages.claim_text_fr: Si la cohabitation comprend des relations sexuelles, l’enseignement catholique les juge comme ayant lieu hors mariage. Si elle est réellement continente, partager un logement n’est pas en soi une fornication, mais il faut encore évaluer l’occasion prochaine, le scandale et le risque qu’une dépendance financière ou affective rende le discernement moins libre.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Prudence requires learning enough before marriage, but not every risk-reduction strategy is morally neutral. Discernment can occur through time, family life, conflict, finances, expectations and chastity without treating marital rights as already possessed.
stages.claim_text_fr: La prudence exige de suffisamment connaître l’autre avant le mariage, mais toute stratégie de réduction du risque n’est pas moralement neutre. Le discernement peut se faire dans le temps, la vie familiale, les conflits, les finances, les attentes et la chasteté sans traiter les droits matrimoniaux comme déjà acquis.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Cohabitation is not one moral category. Sexual cohabitation is direct; chaste co-residence requires prudential case analysis rather than slogans.
stages.claim_text_fr: La cohabitation n’est pas une seule catégorie morale. La cohabitation sexuelle pose un problème direct ; une co-résidence chaste exige une analyse prudentielle du cas.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Traditional moral analysis distinguishes ordinary attraction from deliberately indulged lust.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Neither Aquinas nor the Gospel supplies a numerical second-glance test.

stages.claim_text_en: Simply noticing that someone is attractive is not lust and is not itself sinful. Attraction can arise before the will has consented to anything.
stages.claim_text_fr: Remarquer simplement qu’une personne est attirante n’est pas de la convoitise et n’est pas en soi pécheur. L’attirance peut surgir avant tout consentement de la volonté.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The moral distinction is not the number of glances or how long the eye rests on someone. It is the freely chosen purpose: deliberately looking at a person in order to indulge lust. Merely noticing beauty, even more than once, does not by itself prove interior consent (Mt 5:28; Aquinas, II–II q.154 a.4).
stages.claim_text_fr: La distinction morale ne dépend ni du nombre de regards ni d'une durée précise. Elle tient à l'intention librement choisie : regarder volontairement une personne pour entretenir la convoitise. Remarquer sa beauté, même plus d'une fois, ne prouve pas à soi seul le consentement intérieur (Mt 5, 28 ; saint Thomas, II–II, q.154, a.4).
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: Christ’s teaching on lust directs attention to deliberate interior consent, not merely external adultery. Traditional virtue ethics likewise distinguishes the arising of appetite from the will’s decision to entertain and enjoy it. For someone already dating, engaged or married, repeatedly sexualizing other people can also erode the fidelity one is trying to cultivate.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’enseignement du Christ sur la convoitise vise le consentement intérieur délibéré, non seulement l’adultère extérieur. L’éthique traditionnelle des vertus distingue aussi le surgissement de l’appétit de la décision de la volonté de l’entretenir et de le savourer. Pour une personne déjà en couple, fiancée ou mariée, sexualiser volontairement et de manière répétée d’autres personnes peut aussi éroder la fidélité que l’on cherche à cultiver.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Another person's conduct or clothing can occasion temptation but does not transfer responsibility for one's own deliberate choices. There is no mechanical rule about a 'second glance': the question is whether one knowingly chooses to entertain lust, rather than simply noticing attractiveness.
stages.claim_text_fr: La conduite ou la tenue d'autrui peut occasionner une tentation, sans transférer la responsabilité de ses propres choix délibérés. Il n'existe pas de règle mécanique du « deuxième regard » : la question est de savoir si l'on choisit sciemment d'entretenir la convoitise, plutôt que de simplement remarquer une personne attirante.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: First notice is not the issue. Deliberately looking in order to enjoy lust is.
stages.claim_text_fr: La première perception n’est pas le problème. Regarder délibérément pour jouir de la convoitise l’est.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Marital fidelity governs deliberately cultivated attachments, not involuntary attraction.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Application to unmarried exclusive dating promises is prudent argument, not an encyclical code for dating.

stages.claim_text_en: Friendly charm is not automatically flirtation, and flirtation itself is not defined by a single gesture. Intention, context and relationship matter.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le charme amical n’est pas automatiquement du flirt, et le flirt lui-même ne se définit pas par un geste isolé. L’intention, le contexte et la relation comptent.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The moral problem begins when the person deliberately invites or sustains romantic or sexual interest that he or she has no right to cultivate—especially while promising exclusivity elsewhere.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le problème moral commence lorsqu’une personne suscite ou entretient délibérément un intérêt romantique ou sexuel qu’elle n’a pas le droit de cultiver — surtout lorsqu’elle promet l’exclusivité ailleurs.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: Before marriage, boyfriend/girlfriend or fiancé relationships do not possess all marital rights, but they can contain real promises of exclusivity and honesty. Within marriage, deliberately cultivating a backup romantic bond can violate fidelity before physical adultery occurs. The relevant questions are: what attention am I trying to obtain, what am I encouraging in the other person, and would I act the same way transparently in front of my partner?
stages.claim_text_fr: Avant le mariage, une relation de petit ami/petite amie ou de fiancés ne possède pas tous les droits matrimoniaux, mais elle peut comporter de véritables promesses d’exclusivité et d’honnêteté. Dans le mariage, cultiver délibérément un lien romantique de remplacement peut violer la fidélité avant tout adultère physique. Les questions pertinentes sont : quelle attention est-ce que je cherche ? Qu’est-ce que j’encourage chez l’autre ? Agirais-je de la même manière ouvertement devant mon partenaire ?
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: No. Attraction can be involuntary. Loyalty concerns what one chooses to cultivate, communicate and pursue. The distinction protects against both laxity and jealous control.
stages.claim_text_fr: Non. L’attirance peut être involontaire. La loyauté concerne ce que l’on choisit de cultiver, de communiquer et de poursuivre. Cette distinction protège à la fois du laxisme et du contrôle jaloux.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Flirting becomes disloyal when it deliberately cultivates romantic or sexual attention inconsistent with the relationship one has chosen.
stages.claim_text_fr: Le flirt devient déloyal lorsqu’il cultive délibérément une attention romantique ou sexuelle incompatible avec la relation que l’on a choisie.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Premarital genital sexual acts and ordinary affection differ in moral object.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: No universal catalogue of every act, proximity or private circumstance is promulgated.

stages.claim_text_en: An embrace, kiss or ordinary sign of affection is not intrinsically a grave sexual act. Aquinas, II–II q.154 a.4, explicitly distinguishes such gestures in themselves from gestures deliberately chosen for lustful pleasure. The relevant difference is not merely whether intercourse or orgasm occurs.
stages.claim_text_fr: Une étreinte, un baiser ou une marque ordinaire d'affection ne constitue pas intrinsèquement un acte sexuel grave. Saint Thomas (II–II, q.154, a.4) distingue explicitement ces gestes en eux-mêmes de ceux qui sont délibérément recherchés pour un plaisir de convoitise. La différence ne se réduit pas à la présence d'un rapport conjugal ou d'un orgasme.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The mistake is then treating every act short of intercourse as non-sexual. Oral-genital acts, deliberate genital stimulation, mutual masturbation and rubbing chosen for sexual climax are sexual acts in their own right. Their morality is not changed by the sentence “we did not technically have intercourse.”
stages.claim_text_fr: L’erreur consiste ensuite à traiter tout acte inférieur à la pénétration comme non sexuel. Les actes oro-génitaux, la stimulation génitale délibérée, la masturbation mutuelle et les frottements choisis pour l’orgasme sont des actes sexuels à part entière. Leur moralité ne change pas avec la phrase « nous n’avons pas techniquement eu de rapports ».
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: Engagement prepares for marriage without conferring present conjugal rights (CIC can. 1057). Deliberate genital activity sought for sexual gratification is not made chaste merely by excluding intercourse. Ordinary affection is distinct and calls for prudent discernment, not a catalogue of sexual techniques.
stages.claim_text_fr: Les fiançailles préparent au mariage sans conférer les droits conjugaux présents (CIC, can. 1057). Une activité génitale recherchée pour le plaisir sexuel ne devient pas chaste du seul fait d'éviter le rapport conjugal. L'affection ordinaire est distincte et requiert un discernement prudent, non un catalogue de pratiques sexuelles.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Those are not automatically the same moral act as oral sex or masturbation, but intention is not the only issue. If a couple knowingly creates a situation in which serious sexual sin is predictably likely, the chosen proximate occasion itself becomes morally relevant. A couple that repeatedly loses control should not pretend the setup is neutral because the stated plan was restraint.
stages.claim_text_fr: Ces situations ne sont pas automatiquement le même acte moral que le sexe oral ou la masturbation, mais l’intention n’est pas le seul élément. Si un couple crée sciemment une situation où un péché sexuel grave est prévisiblement probable, l’occasion prochaine choisie devient elle-même moralement pertinente. Un couple qui perd régulièrement le contrôle ne doit pas prétendre que le dispositif est neutre parce que le projet déclaré était la retenue.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Before marriage, “not intercourse” does not equal “not sexual.” Deliberately genital acts belong to the sexual union marriage is meant to contain.
stages.claim_text_fr: Avant le mariage, « pas de pénétration » ne signifie pas « pas sexuel ». Les actes génitaux délibérés appartiennent à l’union sexuelle que le mariage est destiné à contenir.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Manual expressly permits certain non-consummated conjugal affection and condemns non-conjugal completion.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Archived debate; the manual is non-magisterial, uses historical casuistry, and modern accessories lack exhaustive original treatment.

stages.claim_text_en: McHugh and Callan §1624 permits non-consummated acts not only as accessories to lawful intercourse but also as ways of fostering or preserving conjugal love. It does not turn every form of deliberate sexual completion into a lawful marital act.
stages.claim_text_fr: McHugh et Callan (§1624) admettent les actes non consommés non seulement comme accessoires à l’union conjugale licite, mais aussi comme moyens de favoriser ou de préserver l’affection entre époux. Cela ne rend pas licites toutes les formes d’achèvement sexuel délibéré.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The further claim that every consensual form of sexual completion is therefore equivalent does not follow. Traditional manuals distinguish incomplete acts integrated into intercourse from deliberately completed sexual release chosen apart from or as a substitute for the marital act.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’affirmation supplémentaire selon laquelle toute forme consensuelle d’achèvement sexuel serait donc équivalente ne suit pas. Les manuels traditionnels distinguent les actes incomplets intégrés à l’union de la décharge sexuelle délibérément achevée en dehors de l’acte conjugal ou comme substitut à celui-ci.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: McHugh and Callan §1624(a) permits non-consummated acts either as accessories to marital intercourse or to foster and preserve conjugal love, while distinguishing immoderate motives, foreseeable proximate danger of non-conjugal sexual completion, and the presence or absence of sufficient reason. Section 1624(c) rejects sexual completion outside the natural conjugal act. Neither passage is an exhaustive magisterial judgment on every modern device; specific uses require separate examination.
stages.claim_text_fr: McHugh et Callan (§1624 a) permettent les actes non consommés soit comme accessoires de l'union conjugale, soit pour nourrir ou préserver l'amour des époux, tout en distinguant les motifs désordonnés, le danger prochain et prévisible d'un achèvement sexuel non conjugal et l'existence éventuelle d'une raison suffisante. Le §1624 c rejette l'achèvement sexuel hors de l'acte conjugal naturel. Ces passages ne constituent pas un jugement magistériel exhaustif sur tous les dispositifs modernes ; leur usage précis exige un examen distinct.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: The traditional analysis does not deny love; it asks what sexual act the spouses actually choose. A loving motive can accompany different acts, but it does not erase their structure. At the same time, the Church has not defined every modern accessory, so one should not manufacture prohibitions unsupported by the sources.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’analyse traditionnelle ne nie pas l’amour ; elle demande quel acte sexuel les époux choisissent réellement. Un motif aimant peut accompagner des actes différents, mais il n’efface pas leur structure. En même temps, l’Église n’a pas défini chaque accessoire moderne ; il ne faut donc pas fabriquer des interdictions sans appui dans les sources.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Between spouses, non-consummated gestures can express conjugal affection or prepare for intercourse. Deliberately substituting another completed sexual act remains a different moral choice; modern devices call for case-specific assessment, not invented universal prohibitions.
stages.claim_text_fr: Entre époux, des gestes non consommés peuvent exprimer l’affection conjugale ou préparer l’union. Leur substituer délibérément un autre acte sexuel achevé relève d’un choix moral distinct ; les dispositifs modernes exigent un discernement concret, non des interdictions universelles inventées.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.

cases.claim_supported_only_within: Exclusivity of conjugal fidelity cannot be sold, waived or transferred by mutual agreement.
cases.unverified_claim_boundary: Archived scenario remains distinct from consent-as-a-general-concept dossiers.

stages.claim_text_en: An openly agreed arrangement differs morally from a secret affair because deception is absent.
stages.claim_text_fr: Un arrangement ouvertement accepté diffère moralement d’une liaison secrète parce que la tromperie en est absente.
stages.scope_of_review: A limited true premise is conceded; citation does not amount to accepting the opponent's conclusion.

stages.claim_text_en: The unresolved claim is that exclusivity is merely an optional private rule. Catholic marriage treats exclusivity as part of what matrimonial consent establishes, not as a clause spouses may later delete.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’affirmation non démontrée est que l’exclusivité serait une simple règle privée facultative. Le mariage catholique considère l’exclusivité comme partie de ce qu’établit le consentement matrimonial, non comme une clause que les époux peuvent supprimer ensuite.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage states the contested inference; the source can establish principles but not mechanically resolve every application.

stages.claim_text_en: The marital covenant is a mutual, exclusive gift. A spouse cannot authorize the other to treat a third person as a sexual partner without contradicting the form of that covenant.
stages.claim_text_fr: L’alliance matrimoniale est un don mutuel et exclusif. Un conjoint ne peut autoriser l’autre à traiter une tierce personne comme partenaire sexuel sans contredire la forme de cette alliance.
stages.scope_of_review: This is the main doctrinal argument; distinctions between primary teaching and subsidiary empirical premises must be preserved.

stages.claim_text_en: Because Catholicism holds that marriage has an objective structure prior to private preference. The same reason spouses cannot mutually agree to make the bond temporary while still calling it Catholic marriage applies to exclusivity.
stages.claim_text_fr: Parce que le catholicisme soutient que le mariage possède une structure objective antérieure à la préférence privée. La même raison pour laquelle les époux ne peuvent convenir de rendre le lien temporaire tout en l’appelant mariage catholique vaut pour l’exclusivité.
stages.scope_of_review: This stage answers a further objection; philosophical or pastoral applications must remain distinguishable from original quotations.

stages.claim_text_en: Mutual permission removes deception, not the contradiction with marital exclusivity.
stages.claim_text_fr: La permission mutuelle supprime la tromperie, non la contradiction avec l’exclusivité matrimoniale.
stages.scope_of_review: The conclusion synthesizes reasoning and may not be presented as a literal source quotation.
